records.label: Four unrelated individuals with FGFR3 Lys650Met

phenotypes.text: severe skeletal dysplasia approaching thanatophoric dysplasia type I severity
extensive acanthosis nigricans beginning in early childhood

quotes: We have identified a novel fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3) missense mutation in four unrelated individuals with skeletal dysplasia that approaches the severity observed in thanatophoric dysplasia type I (TD1).

However, three of the four individuals developed extensive areas of acanthosis nigricans beginning in early childhood, suffer from severe neurological impairments, and have survived past infancy without prolonged life-support measures.

records.label: SADDAN patients with FGFR3 Lys650Met

phenotypes.text: severe disturbance of endochondral bone growth
reverse (posterior apex) tibial and fibular bowing
ram's horn bowing of the clavicle

quotes: We previously discovered a novel missense mutation (Lys650Met) in the tyrosine kinase domain of the fibroblast growth factor receptor 3 (FGFR3) gene in four unrelated individuals
Other unusual bone deformities, such as femoral bowing with reverse (i.e., posterior apex) tibial and fibular bowing and "ram's horn" bowing of the clavicle, are also seen in some patients.

In addition to skeletal dysplasia, progressive acanthosis nigricans, and central nervous system structural anomalies, seizures and severe developmental delays are observed in surviving SADDAN patients.

records.label: Patient with SADDAN
quotes: We present prenatal and postnatal features of a patient with severe achondroplasia with developmental delay and acanthosis nigricans (SADDAN). Mutation analysis confirmed the clinical diagnosis by detecting the FGFR3 Lys650Met mutation.
confirms the severe morbidity and adds to the reports with early mortality associated with SADDAN

notes.statement: Zankl et al. (2008) reviewed the clinical and radiologic features of all reported cases of SADDAN. They noted that their case was one of only six with molecular analysis reported in the literature, and that it supported the severe morbidity and early mortality linked to SADDAN.
quotes: This case, one of only six with molecular analysis reported in the literature, confirms the severe morbidity and adds to the reports with early mortality associated with SADDAN.
Clinical-radiological characteristics of all reported cases of SADDAN are reviewed and discussed.

notes.statement: Iwata et al. (2001) introduced the K644M point mutation, corresponding to human FGFR3 K650M, into the mouse Fgfr3 gene. Heterozygous mutant mice showed a phenotype similar to human SADDAN, with the majority surviving the perinatal period, suggesting that the survival of SADDAN patients is indeed attributable to the K650M mutation. Long bone abnormalities were milder than in the TDII mouse model, and overgrowth of cartilaginous tissues was observed in the rib cartilage, trachea, and nasal septum.
quotes: To find out whether the K650M mutation also causes the SADDAN phenotype, we introduced the corresponding point mutation (K644M) into the mouse Fgfr3 gene. Heterozygous mutant mice show a phenotype similar to human SADDAN, e.g. the majority of the SADDAN mice survive the perinatal period.
The long bone abnormalities in SADDAN mice are milder than the TDII model. In addition, overgrowth of the cartilaginous tissues is observed in the rib cartilage, trachea and nasal septum.

notes.statement: Iwata et al. (2001) found that FGF ligand at low concentration differentially activated MAP kinase in primary chondrocyte cultures from wildtype and SADDAN mice.
quotes: The FGF ligand at the low concentration differentially activates Map kinase in primary chondrocyte cultures from wild-type and SADDAN mice.

notes.statement: Iwata et al. (2001) noted that although FGFR3 with the SADDAN K650M mutation is more activated in vitro than FGFR3 with the TDII K650E mutation, TDII is lethal at birth whereas most SADDAN patients survive the perinatal period.
quotes: TDII is lethal at birth, whereas most of the SADDAN patients survive the perinatal period. However, FGFR3 with the SADDAN mutation is more activated than FGFR3 with the TDII mutation in vitro.

notes.statement: Bellus et al. (1999) found that the FGFR3 Lys650Met mutation caused severe disturbances in endochondral bone growth approaching and overlapping those of thanatophoric dysplasia type I, but that it was most often compatible with survival into adulthood.
quotes: The FGFR3 Lys650Met mutation results in severe disturbances in endochondral bone growth that approach and overlap those observed in thanatophoric dysplasia, type I. However, this mutation is most often compatible with survival into adulthood.

notes.statement: Bellus et al. (1999) noted that although Lys650Met lies in the same FGFR3 codon as the thanatophoric dysplasia type II mutation Lys650Glu and has a similar effect on constitutive activation of the FGFR3 tyrosine kinase, it is not associated with cloverleaf skull or craniosynostosis.
quotes: Despite its location within the same FGFR3 codon as the thanatophoric dysplasia type II mutation (Lys650Glu) and a similar effect on constitutive activation of the FGFR3 tyrosine kinase, the Lys650Met is not associated with cloverleaf skull or craniosynostosis.

notes.statement: Tavormina et al. (1999) performed transient transfection studies with FGFR3 mutant constructs. These showed that the Lys650Met mutation causes a dramatic increase in constitutive receptor kinase activity, about three times greater than that seen with the Lys650Glu mutation found in TD2.
quotes: Transient transfection studies with FGFR3 mutant constructs show that the Lys650Met mutation causes a dramatic increase in constitutive receptor kinase activity, approximately three times greater than that observed with the Lys650Glu mutation.

notes.statement: Tavormina et al. (1999) found that the FGFR3 mutation A1949T (Lys650Met) lies at the nucleotide next to the TD2 mutation (A1948G, Lys650Glu). It produces a different amino acid substitution at a highly conserved codon in the activation loop of the kinase domain.
quotes: The FGFR3 mutation (A1949T: Lys650Met) occurs at the nucleotide adjacent to the TD type II (TD2) mutation (A1948G: Lys650Glu) and results in a different amino acid substitution at a highly conserved codon in the kinase domain activation loop.

notes.statement: Tavormina et al. (1999) named the phenotype caused by the FGFR3 Lys650Met mutation 'severe achondroplasia with developmental delay and acanthosis nigricans' (SADDAN). They chose a separate name because it differs significantly from the phenotypes of other known FGFR3 mutations.
quotes: We refer to the phenotype caused by the Lys650Met mutation as "severe achondroplasia with developmental delay and acanthosis nigricans" (SADDAN) because it differs significantly from the phenotypes of other known FGFR3 mutations.
